records.content: Review some of the top stories from the Contemporary Pediatrics website over the last week, and catch up on anything you may have missed. Thank you for visiting the Contemporary Pediatrics® website. Take a look at some of our top stories from last week (Monday, November 2 to Friday, November 6, 2026) and click each link to read and watch anything you may have missed. 1.) First pediatric flu death of the 2026-27 season The CDC reported the 2026-27 season's first influenza-associated pediatric death, in a child who died during the week ending October 10 from illness linked to influenza A(H1N1); FluView did not disclose the child's age, location, or vaccination status. A second pediatric death reported for the week ending October 24 was a late-reported influenza B case from September that raised the 2025-26 season's pediatric total to 199. San Bernardino County, California, separately announced on October 30 the flu-related death of a child with underlying conditions who was too young to be vaccinated, and Colorado confirmed its first pediatric flu death of the season in mid-October. For the week ending October 24, 7.6% of more than 53,000 clinical specimens tested positive for influenza, with 98.9% of subtyped influenza A viruses identified as A(H1N1)pdm09; children aged 0-4 had the second-highest hospitalization rate (1.8 per 100,000) of any age group, and FluSurv-NET's weekly hospitalization rate is the highest for this point in a season since 2010-11. CDC estimates at least 1 million illnesses, 16,000 hospitalizations, and 900 deaths so far this season, though the agency cautions that seasonal activity remains low nationally overall and that death counts often rise as reporting catches up. 2.) Skipping newborn vitamin K tied to 47% higher infant bleeding risk A retrospective JAMA cohort of roughly 5.24 million US infants born at 35 to 43 weeks' gestation from 2017 to 2025, drawn from Epic Cosmos EHR data, found that infants who did not receive the standard intramuscular vitamin K injection faced significantly higher bleeding risk. Nonreceipt of the shot more than doubled over the study period, from 3.1% in 2017 to 6.8% in 2025, and 4.5% of infants overall (234,825) did not receive it. Bleeding by 6 months occurred in 288.0 per 10,000 nonrecipients versus 185.9 per 10,000 recipients, an adjusted risk ratio of 1.47; intracranial bleeding risk was more than double (adjusted risk ratio 2.43), and the risk of death with concurrent bleeding during the birth hospitalization was nearly triple (adjusted risk ratio 2.69). Because the design is retrospective and observational, the authors note it shows association rather than causation, and they could not determine whether some "nonrecipients" had instead received oral vitamin K or a later injection; accompanying commentary called for reinforced vitamin K recommendations and dedicated surveillance. 3.) Study identifies gaps in infant RSV immunization timing A retrospective cohort poster presented at IDWeek 2026 examined 80,862 infants born between April 2025 and March 2026 across a national network of primary care clinics, of whom 17,771 received the RSV monoclonal antibody nirsevimab (Beyfortus). Among infants born during RSV season, only 35.4% were immunized within the recommended 7-day window after birth, and the median time to administration was 14 days. Timing varied by insurance type: for in-season births, the median time to administration was 27 days for self-pay infants compared with 14 days for commercially insured infants and 13 days for those covered by Medicaid or the Vaccines for Children program, a gap the researchers linked to insurance-rostering delays rather than to access itself. The analysis covered only outpatient administration and could not capture doses given in birth hospitals, so the authors caution it cannot establish overall nirsevimab coverage; they suggest proactive scheduling, caregiver education, and reminder systems to close the timing gaps. 4.) Cenobamate sNDAs seek PGTC and pediatric focal seizure indications Two supplemental new drug applications for cenobamate (Xcopri) are now before the FDA: one seeking a primary generalized tonic-clonic (PGTC) seizure indication for patients 12 and older, and a second, submitted in October, seeking a pediatric focal-onset seizure indication. Cenobamate is currently approved in the US only for partial-onset seizures in adults. The PGTC application rests on a phase 3 trial of 169 patients, including 34 adolescents aged 12 to 17, in which median PGTC seizure frequency fell 71.9% with cenobamate versus 39.6% with placebo. During the 12-week maintenance phase, 43.4% of cenobamate-treated patients were seizure-free compared with 20.5% on placebo, though treatment-emergent adverse events, mainly somnolence and fatigue, occurred in 60.0% of cenobamate patients versus 53.0% on placebo. The efficacy data so far come from sponsor-authored conference abstracts rather than a peer-reviewed publication; outcomes for the adolescent subgroup were not reported separately, and the company has not disclosed FDA target action dates for either application. 5.) What new dietary guidelines mean for pediatric practice Speaking at the AAP 2026 National Conference & Exhibition, Natalie D. Muth, MD, MPH, RDN, MBA, told pediatricians that the 2025-2030 Dietary Guidelines for Americans do not require major changes to routine nutrition counseling, despite several shifts in emphasis. The guidelines place more weight on animal protein, and Muth cautioned against discouraging plant-based proteins, which she said remain healthy; they also favor whole milk over reduced-fat options for children, a recommendation she noted the AAP and other organizations have not necessarily adopted. For the first time, the guidelines explicitly address ultra-processed and highly processed foods, giving pediatricians an opening to discuss reducing them when feasible. Muth recommended open-ended questions and small, achievable changes rather than strict rules, and acknowledged that the evidence on dairy fat specifically is mixed; she also noted that food access and family circumstances limit how well any dietary recommendation can be followed in practice

Many densely populated areas in California offer free or reduced costs for vaccines in the months leading up to influenza and COVID-19 season. “Even if vaccines are free and available to me, that doesn’t mean they’re equally accessible to everyone,” said Evelyn Wang, a high school sophomore in the East Bay. A single cough lasts a second. The sound disappears into the chatter of a classroom, swallowed by the next conversation, the next bell, or the next lesson. But the virus behind it may continue its journey long after the cough is forgotten, weaving between people, through hallways, and leaving a secret mark on everyone in sight. Every year, thousands of students get sick, passing viruses through school halls, transmitting germs on shared supplies, and spreading illnesses across stuffy classrooms. The seasonal cycle of sickness is routine for many high schoolers, anticipated as a winter hurdle that peaks well into the school year. However, many students are falling ill much earlier than expected, dealing with spiking fevers and coughing fits that lead to unexpected absences. This shift hints at a broader trend in California. An unseasonal surge in respiratory illness, arriving almost two months early, is forcing students out of classrooms weeks before the typical start of the sick season, disrupting teachers’ lesson plans, and causing alarm among immunologists. Behind the virus Influenza, more commonly known as the flu, and COVID-19 are common respiratory diseases that affect the lungs and nasal passages. Understanding how influenza and COVID-19 spread and how to protect against them is complex. “Viruses are pretty simple organisms, but they find ways to evade capture, changing a little bit every year,” said Jennifer Klein, an allergy immunologist at Kaiser Hayward. “That’s why you have to change the vaccine to recognize the strain in the community.” Two main types of influenza, A and B, cause seasonal flu epidemics in humans. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), influenza B causes fever, cough, sore throat, runny nose, headaches, fatigue, and potentially vomiting. Influenza A has a higher mutation rate, similar symptoms to influenza B, and affects more age groups. COVID-19 is caused by SARS-CoV-2, which can result in fever, chills, dry cough, fatigue, loss of taste or smell, sore throat, and congestion. COVID-19 spreads through airborne droplets when people sneeze, cough, or talk. According to the American Psychological Association, teenagers have a lower risk perception of COVID-19 and the flu, often underestimating their vulnerability and the severity of the illness. “There is information available about vaccines, especially online and in pharmacies, but it doesn’t always reach people. Sometimes, information can be confusing or conflicting, especially when it comes from unreliable sources,” said Evelyn Wang, a high school sophomore in the East Bay. As California heads into the peak of the flu and COVID-19 seasons, regional transmission varies. Early arrival This year’s flu and COVID-19 season arrived earlier and proved more severe than in previous years, according to the California Department of Public Health (CDPH). Currently, influenza A is more dominant than influenza B in California, and hospitalizations are 11 times higher this year than during the same week last year. Wenxian Fu, an immunologist who previously worked at Genentech and the University of California, San Diego, said virus trends come down to weather and people staying inside more. “In the winter, it’s more likely for flu and COVID-19 to spread because the weather’s colder, and so the virus replicates more easily,” Fu said. According to CNN, another major reason for the spike in cases earlier in the season is a new mutation of influenza A. This new mutation, G155E, carries a genetic tweak that originated in Asia, allowing the virus to replicate and spread more easily. Because the strain emerged almost two months before the predicted date, many people have not yet had the chance to get vaccinated against it, according to KQED. Additionally, the CDPH said that this year’s season will be prolonged and may hit a “double wave,” with a second surge of influenza and COVID-19 later in winter or early spring. San Francisco has recorded its first flu-related death of the season. Inside the shot The active ingredient in most vaccines is called an antigen. Antigens typically trigger the immune system to learn to defend against diseases if people do get infected. Many people feel mild discomfort or tiredness for a day or two after getting a vaccine, but the resulting protection lasts for months. When a vaccine mimics the infection, it engages the body’s natural defenses, training it for when the real disease arrives. Immunity takes a few weeks to develop, and people can still get infected in the weeks that follow. Still, a vaccinated person is far less likely to become seriously ill than someone who is unvaccinated. “I still get yearly shots for the flu because it keeps changing, but I don’t really know how COVID-19 is going to change because I haven’t been following it,” said Louis Au, a sophomore in Irvine, California. In a study investigating vaccine hesitancy among youth, up to 58% of adolescents are hesitant to get vaccinated due to needle phobia, believing they are healthy enough to skip it, distrust of the need for vaccination, or dislike of the symptoms vaccines cause. “People do legitimately feel bad after they get something like the seasonal flu or COVID-19 vaccine, and we don’t deny that it happens. We try to emphasize that it’s actually a good thing because it shows the vaccine is doing its job, and that it’s a lot better than actually meeting that virus for the first time,” Klein said. The importance of vaccines is clear. A study published in the Journal of the American Medical Association said that between December 2020 and October 2024, COVID-19 vaccines alone prevented around 2.5 million deaths. “Every year, the virus evolves in different versions, so when someone gets infected, the symptoms range. The protection someone gained from vaccines in previous years won’t always carry over to the next year, so it’s important to get vaccinated every year,” Fu said. Beating the bug There are many ways to stay ahead of influenza and COVID-19. The main one is through vaccination for the general public. According to the California Health Care Foundation, more than 11.2 million California residents lack easy access to primary care or a place to get vaccinated. “Look to drugstores or community health centers such as Planned Parenthood for vaccines. You can also get information from places like the CDC website or your county health system’s website to give you a sense of what’s going on,” Klein said. For students, staying protected from viruses looks a bit different. Students who spend all day in poorly ventilated classrooms and get less sleep are more susceptible to catching viruses. “Try to have a good daily routine, get enough sleep, drink water, try to eat vitamin C-rich food, and stay home if you’re feeling sick,” Fu said. “Don’t be scared of viruses, but don’t overlook them either.” View Story Comments Share on Facebook Share on X Email this Story Print this Story Navigate Left News Flight training costs take off on the Peninsula News California driving test pass rates decrease in recent years News Upcoming California law impacts teen social media usage News New synthetic opioid variant surfaces in Bay Area News France’s student protests put the education system under pressure News In Photos: Goblin Walk fills downtown San Carlos with Halloween spirit News Human actions continue to move species toward extinction News National park funding concerns extend beyond park boundaries News California data breach affects millions of students News Belmont voters face tax decision on Barrett Community Center Navigate Right About the Contributor Ella Lee-Donley, Staff Writer Ella Lee-Donley (Class of 2029) is a sophomore at Carlmont and a first-year journalist. Hospitals across the Kathmandu Valley are reporting more patients with respiratory illnesses as temperatures fall and air pollution worsens, with doctors warning that vulnerable groups face a higher risk of severe complications. Post File Photo bookmark facebook twitter Whatsapp mail Arjun Poudel Published at : November 7, 2026 Updated at : November 7, 2026 07:39 Kathmandu As temperatures begin to drop and the post-monsoon dry season sets in, hospitals in the Kathmandu Valley have begun reporting an increase in patients with respiratory illnesses, influenza, coughs and fever. Doctors warn that respiratory illnesses could rise further after next week’s Tihar festival as falling temperatures and increasing air pollution aggravate respiratory problems, while festival gatherings also create opportunities for respiratory viruses to spread. “Of the total number of patients seeking care in our hospital these days, around 50 percent are those suffering from respiratory illnesses, colds, coughs, and fever,” said Dr Raju Pangeni, a consultant pulmonary and critical care physician at Hams Hospital. “Some patients also seek care only after they become serious at home. We have to admit such patients at the intensive care unit upon arrival.” Other hospitals in the Valley are reporting a similar increase in patients with respiratory illnesses. Doctors say seasonal influenza is highly contagious and spreads easily. Adults may not be severely affected from the infection, but elderly people, children, and those with underlying health complications are at risk of getting severe, they added. “Of the over 500 patients seeking care in our hospital every day, over 50 percent come with cold, fever, and respiratory illnesses,” said Dr Ramhari Chapagain, director at the Kanti Children’s Hospital. “Some parents bring their children to the hospital only when their condition deteriorates. We have been urging parents not to wait too long at home before seeking medical attention.” Doctors say seasonal influenza affects the respiratory system and spreads quickly within communities. They warn that it can lead to complications including pneumonia, which can be fatal, especially among vulnerable groups. Pneumonia, an infection of the lungs caused by various types of bacteria, viruses and fungi, is the leading cause of death among children under five in Nepal. It kills more children annually than malaria, tuberculosis, and HIV combined. According to the World Health Organisation, pneumonia accounts for 15 percent of under-five mortality in the world. Doctors say pneumonia caused by bacteria is deadlier than that caused by viruses, and children under five and people above 65 years of age are particularly vulnerable to severe illness. Seasonal influenza can affect people of all ages, but those with comorbidities and the elderly are at higher risk of complications. Its symptoms include fever, cough, body aches, and in some cases, vomiting, diarrhoea, and pneumonia. According to Dr Chapagain, diarrheal cases have also risen alongside respiratory diseases. There is no system in place to monitor influenza infections, their severity, and deaths, because not all patients seek hospital care or undergo testing. Also, not all health facilities maintain records or report cases to the authorities. Doctors also say testing is not routinely necessary, as there is no specific treatment for seasonal influenza. Health experts estimate that thousands of people in Nepal get infected with influenza every year. They urge the public to get the influenza vaccine, especially elderly people, children, and those with underlying health conditions. “We don’t know exactly how many people contract seasonal influenza, develop severe symptoms, or die from it each year in Nepal,” said Dr Anup Subedee, an infectious disease expert. “However, based on the number of patients admitted to intensive care units with severe infections, we can assume that a few thousand people may die from influenza every year. So it is better to get vaccinated against the virus.” Experts say early diagnosis is crucial for preventing infection and complications. Patients recover early if treated promptly. Dr Sher Bahadur Pun, chief of the Clinical Research Unit at the Teku-based Sukraraj Tropical and Infectious Disease Hospital, also stresses the risk for vulnerable groups. “Those suffering from heart ailments, renal problems, cancer, and diabetes, as well as elderly people and children, are highly vulnerable to getting severe,” he said. “At the very least, these groups should be administered the influenza vaccine. Health care workers, who get exposed to the infected patients, should also get vaccinated.” Sukraraj is the government-run hospital and national referral hospital for infectious diseases. Public health measures—mask-wearing, handwashing, avoiding crowds, and maintaining social distancing—can reduce infection, doctors say. Arjun Poudel Arjun Poudel is a health reporter for The Kathmandu Post. Before joining the Post, he worked for Sagarmatha Television, Naya Patrika, Republica and The Himalayan Times. records.content: メインコンテンツへスキップ Photo byyuuko01 2026 Influenza: An 'Early Outbreak.' Get Vaccinated to Prepare for the Second Wave たぁぼ Nov 6, 2026 08:39 Table of Contents 1. The second earliest start on record Why did it break out so early? 2. The current dominant strain is A(H1N1)pdm09 Symptoms 3. This season is a 'slow-burn' outbreak 4. A second wave is possible between January and March 2027 Be especially careful during the year-end and New Year holidays 5. 'Vaccination' is the most effective way to prepare for the second wave 6. Infection control measures you can take now besides vaccination Hand washing, gargling, and ventilation すべて表示 The 2026 influenza season began in August, significantly earlier than in typical years. While Type A is currently dominant, there is a possibility that a second wave caused by a different strain could arrive after the new year. This article explains the background of this early outbreak and the preparations you can make now, starting with vaccination. 1. The second earliest start on record The 2026 influenza season began nationwide in late August. This is the second earliest pace since 1999, following 2009. In typical years, the peak of the outbreak is between December and March, but this year, the number of patients began to increase from the end of summer. Due to the early start, infections are spreading more easily in schools and workplaces. Why did it break out so early? Factors such as poor physical condition and fatigue due to prolonged rain, difficulty in ventilating rooms, and an increase in human movement are considered to be in the background. It has also been pointed out that the earlier timing of vaccination may be related to the early onset of the outbreak. 2. The current dominant strain is A(H1N1)pdm09 The strain circulating in the 2026 season is mainly the A(H1N1)pdm09 subtype. In recent detection data, Type A is overwhelmingly common, while the proportion of Type B remains low. Type A is characterized by high infectivity and a tendency for the number of patients to increase in a short period. Caution is especially needed in places with frequent close contact, such as at home, in the workplace, and at school. Symptoms Fever, headache, joint pain, general malaise, cough, and sore throat are the main symptoms. While similar to a cold, influenza is characterized by a sudden high fever and strong systemic symptoms. 3. This season is a 'slow-burn' outbreak This year's outbreak is not the type where the number of patients increases all at once, but rather a 'slow-burn' type that repeatedly increases and decreases. Therefore, it is premature to feel relieved that the outbreak is over just because the number of reports has temporarily decreased. In the past two seasons, the peak was reached about 8 weeks after the start of the outbreak, but this year, it has continued to fluctuate. For this reason, there is a possibility that the risk of infection will continue for a long period in the future. 4. A second wave is possible between January and March 2027 Experts predict that after the first peak in October and November, there is a possibility of a second wave arriving between January and March 2027. Apart from the Type A strain that circulated in the first wave, there is a possibility of an outbreak caused by a different strain, such as A(H3N2) or Type B. Last season, after Type A circulated in the autumn, Type B spread again in the latter half of winter. Be especially careful during the year-end and New Year holidays During the year-end and New Year holidays, contact with others increases due to homecoming, travel, and year-end parties. Cold and dry weather also add to the situation, making it a time when infections are likely to re-expand. If you want to prepare for the second wave, it is important to have your preparations in place by the end of the year. 5. 'Vaccination' is the most effective way to prepare for the second wave The most important thing in preparing for the second wave is getting the influenza vaccine. While the vaccine does not completely prevent the onset of the disease, it is expected to be effective in reducing the risk of severe illness and hospitalization. In particular, we recommend early vaccination for the following people: • Elderly people • Small children • Pregnant women • People with underlying conditions such as asthma or diabetes • People working in medical and nursing care settings • People who have elderly people or small children in their family Since it takes about two weeks for antibodies to develop after vaccination, it is ideal to get vaccinated from the end of the year to early in the new year to be in time for the second wave. 6. Infection control measures you can take now besides vaccination Along with vaccination, it is important to continue daily infection control measures. Hand washing, gargling, and ventilation Washing your hands when returning home and before meals, gargling appropriately, and frequent ventilation are basic measures. Hand sanitizing is also effective when you are out. Wearing a mask Try to wear a mask in crowds or poorly ventilated places. If you have a cough or sore throat, wearing a mask is important to prevent infecting those around you. Health management Lack of sleep and fatigue lower your immune system. Getting enough sleep, eating a balanced diet, and staying properly hydrated are ways to prevent illness. 7. Seek medical attention early if you develop a fever If you develop a fever or severe fatigue, do not force yourself to go to work or school, and consult a medical institution as soon as possible. Starting anti-influenza medication within 48 hours of onset can shorten the duration of the fever and may reduce the amount of virus shed. Early medical consultation is especially important for the elderly, those with underlying conditions, pregnant women, and small children. When to seek medical attention Do not hesitate to see a doctor if you experience any of the following: • High fever of 39°C or higher that persists • Fever lasting 3 days or more • Difficulty breathing or chest pain • Clouded consciousness or convulsions • Inability to drink fluids or decreased urination Summary The 2026 influenza season began at the very early time of late August. Currently, the A(H1N1)pdm09 strain is dominant, but there is a possibility of a second wave caused by a different strain after the turn of the year. The peak of the second wave is expected to be around January to March 2027. Getting vaccinated early and continuing basic measures such as hand washing, ventilation, and wearing masks are the keys to preventing infection and severe illness. The initiative, held at the Gulf News premises, was coordinated with InsuranceMarket.ae and featured a medical team from Dr. Sulaiman Al Habib Hospital. Dubai: With flu cases on the rise, Gulf News has organised a complimentary flu vaccination drive for its employees, reinforcing its commitment to staff health and well-being. Held at the Gulf News premises on November 4, the initiative has been conducted in coordination with InsuranceMarket.ae, with a medical team from Dr. Sulaiman Al Habib Hospital administering the vaccines. The campaign has encouraged employees to take preventive steps against seasonal influenza while helping create a safer and healthier working environment for everyone. Protecting employees and their families The Gulf News HR Department has noted that employee health and well-being remain a priority, particularly during the flu season. The initiative has also extended beyond the workplace, helping protect colleagues, family members, and loved ones by reducing the risk of spreading infections. Keeping frontline distribution teams protected For Gulf News' circulation and distribution department, vaccination has been particularly important given the nature of its employees’ daily work. Potru Raju, director of circulation sales and distribution at Gulf News, has bared that the department has around 300 newspaper delivery staff, also known as GN news boys, and about 30 van drivers who interact with subscribers and fellow riders every day. “Our distribution team handles several deliveries every day where they face subscribers and fellow riders. We are thankful to Gulf News, HR department, and our CEO, for organising this flu vaccination,” said Raju. He has also thanked Dr. Sulaiman Al Habib Hospital for providing a friendly and helpful medical team. “This is very important because these are my staff and we are grateful that Gulf News always takes care of their employees.” Why getting vaccinated matters Dr. Arwa Alhaj, general practitioner at Dr. Sulaiman Al Habib Hospital, has urged people to get vaccinated against influenza, explaining that the vaccine can help reduce the severity of the illness. Flu symptoms can vary from person to person and vaccination can help make the infection milder if a person catches the virus. “Take a flu vaccine. Don't be confused about that because it will help you a lot to prevent the flu or influenza,” Alhaj told Gulf News. She has highlighted the role of prevention in reducing the risk of complications and hospital admissions. "Are you afraid of taking the vaccine or being admitted to the hospital? Better to take the flu vaccine to prevent this admission and to prevent worsening coming after the flu infection." A shared commitment to preventive healthcare Rahul Kumar, VIP account manager at InsuranceMarket.ae, has mentioned that supporting employee vaccination was a vital part of promoting preventive healthcare. "It is important for us to help them so that their employees have proper vaccination throughout the year," stated Kumar. He has described the annual flu vaccination as a precautionary measure as seasons change, adding that people who regularly interact with others should take steps to protect themselves and those around them. For her part, Sumavathi Kotian, business development manager at GIG Gulf, has stressed the relevance of prevention. "Having prevention as the first step is necessary. Having a flu vaccine is important because it supports your health from the upcoming flu and prevents unnecessary visits to the provider," said Kotian. She has underscored that vaccines help support the body’s immune system in responding to viruses, including those that change over time. In addition, Kotian has pointed out that flu vaccination is a preventive measure that can benefit both individual health and the wider healthcare system by helping reduce avoidable medical visits and claims. Making workplace health a priority The vaccination drive has reflected the collaboration between employers, healthcare providers, and insurance partners in promoting preventive healthcare. By making flu vaccines accessible to employees at the workplace, Gulf News has formed a culture of prevention and ensured staff have an opportunity to protect their health during the flu season. The initiative has also demonstrated how simple preventive measures can contribute to the well-being of employees, their families, and the wider community they serve. records.content: 顶部 首页 首页 晴 / 9° 隐私 四价流感疫苗去哪儿了?WHO砍掉的毒株,压垮了一家上市公司 MedTrend医趋势 深入探索 探索同城攻略 查阅世界地图 阅读旅游攻略 又到秋冬季,近期疾控中心提醒当前已进入流感流行季,预计11月底至12月起流感进入上升通道。从流行毒株看,甲流为主、乙流为辅。甲流阳性样本中,甲型H3N2占比近七成,甲型H1N1占比三成。 今年打流感疫苗,你可能发现找不到四价了——不是缺货,是四价退场了。 深入探索 预约汽车试驾 体验极速搜索 发现精彩活动 由于乙型Yamagata系病毒自2020年3月起再未被全球监测到,世界卫生组织建议将其从疫苗组分中移除,全球流感疫苗已全面转向三价。 这场调整背后,是整个行业的洗牌:毒株更替、增值税率上调、集采压价多重因素叠加,有人巨亏,有人掉队,也有人逆势翻盘。 展开剩余 88 % 01、传统流感疫苗赛道的适配阵痛 根据中国疾控中心发布的《中国流感疫苗预防接种技术指南(2026—2027)》,本年度推荐的三种疫苗组分均进行了更新,包括三价裂解疫苗、三价亚单位疫苗和三价减毒活疫苗。 如果说其他品种还在逐步修复,传统流感疫苗赛道则继续承受冲击。毒株调整、税制变化、价格管控多重因素叠加,一些企业由盈转亏。 受甲型H3N2、乙型Victoria毒株变异影响,2026年流感疫苗批签发启动时间普遍晚于往年,7月进入集中签发期,季节性供应特征显著,全年供应重心集中在下半年。 从今年流感疫苗签发数量来看,截至10月, 流感病毒裂解疫苗(为绝对主流品类,签发的几乎都是三价):华兰生物38批;北京科兴37批;复星雅立峰19批;智飞龙科马生物16批;赛诺菲10批;上海生物制品8批;天元生物7批;长春生物5批;武汉生物3批。 流感病毒亚单位疫苗:江苏中慧元通28批;中逸安科生物21批。 鼻喷流感减毒活疫苗:百克生物独家12批。 作为传统流感疫苗领域的头部企业,华兰疫苗今年前三季度的业绩出现明显波动。营收3.01亿元,同比下降62.67%;归母净利润由盈转亏,为-445.11万元,同比下滑103.36%;扣非净利润亏损3710.19万元,同比下降143.01%。 主要原因包括: 税制层面,根据财政部税务总局2026年第10号公告,自今年1月1日起,血液制品、疫苗制品不再适用3%增值税简易征收政策,统一执行13%的一般计税模式,税率上调直接拉低了不含税收入口径,也加重了成本端压力。 市场及价格方面的影响更为直接。随着WHO推荐疫苗组分剔除B/Yamagata系病毒,本流感季主流产品由四价转为三价,终端定价随之调整;同时公司深度参与农村“一老一小”免费接种项目,疫苗以政策性优惠价供应,河南、安徽等地政府采购中标价低至9元/支。 而金迪克更因产品结构过于单一,在本轮调整中或将面临退市风险。 其前三季度营收仅92.05万元,同比下降98.77%;归母净利润亏损8938.06万元,亏损幅度同比扩大3.37%;其中单三季度营收不足万元,同比下滑99.99%。公司同时在三季报中提示,初步测算全年营业收入可能低于1亿元且无法扭亏,或将触及财务类退市风险警示。 业绩大幅下滑的核心原因是产品断档,错过了今年的销售窗口期。 金迪克此前的收入几乎全部来自四价流感疫苗,但随着B/Yamagata系毒株被剔除出推荐组分,本流感季四价产品不再销售;而公司的三价流感疫苗直到今年9月底才获批,暂无可供销售的产品。 其实,自2021年上市以来,金迪克的净利润已连续多年下滑,2023年泰州暴雨淹厂、2024-2025流感季批签发滞后,都对业绩造成了持续冲击。 02、减亏账里的不同底色,海外、差异化新品发力 智飞、康希诺、康泰、康华、百克净利润实现增长。 首先是,中国最大的疫苗厂商智飞生物,虽然前三季度整体依然亏损,但从2024年下半年开始的净利润下滑终于止住了,净亏损收窄约49%。且2026年第三季度单季,公司归母净利润1.25亿元,同比增长117.36%。这也是2024年下半年以来的首个单季度盈利。 二级市场也随之给予积极反馈,从财报公布以来已经连涨了四天。 从智飞生物的营收来看同比下滑14.46%,所以盈利并不是来自于产品销售。 首先财务因素的贡献占了大头。去年同期计提的存货跌价和坏账,到今年基数大幅降低;存货跌价损失同比改善了3.3亿元,信用减值损失(应收账款坏账)也少计提了1.04亿元,两项合计为利润贡献了4亿多元的增量。 与之配套且值得欣慰的是库存大幅出清。期末存货从年初的50.03亿元降到20.03亿元,差不多砍掉了六成;曾经压在账上的减值隐患,已经随着库存消化逐步释放。 再加上销售费用同比压缩了近四分之一,管理费用同比-6.60%,研发费用基本持平。这些都是降本带来的利好。 此外,今年4月和默沙东调整了采购协议,从之前的刚性基础采购改成按市场需动态采购,相当于从根源上解除了高价囤货的机制性风险。 截至目前,智飞生物仍有超过89%的营收还是来自于代理外资品牌(默沙东、GSK)的疫苗,自主产品仅占不到10%。 从2026年签发数量手动统计来看,1月—10月批签发批次,默沙东的23价肺炎球菌多糖疫苗:1批;口服五价重配轮状病毒减毒活疫苗(进口):合计24批;九价人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)疫苗(酿酒酵母,进口):2批。 智飞生物代理的GSK产品只有重组带状疱疹疫苗(欣安立适,CHO细胞),并保留RSV疫苗(Arexvy)的优先合作权。而2026年截至目前,欣安立适共签发了0批。 根据智飞生物解释,代理的疫苗签发减少,是公司主动暂停采购、消化历史库存的战略安排。 康希诺前三季度营收同比增27.4%,增速位居榜首。 营收增长来自双轮驱动。一是海外业务爆发,上半年海外收入同比暴增47倍多,前三季度延续放量,主要通过向印尼供应PCV13i疫苗中间品、提供工艺研发服务实现;二是新品管线扩容,今年新获批的三组分百白破“盼康欣”等产品,在多个省份准入。 具体来看,2026年1月—10月疫苗批签发: 13价肺炎球菌多糖结合疫苗3批。 ACYW135群脑膜炎球菌多糖结合疫苗24批。 A群C群脑膜炎球菌多糖结合疫苗1批。 吸附无细胞百(三组分)白破联合疫苗1批。 但是,其前三季度归母净利润为正主要依靠的是3964万元国际专项研发补助,扣非后实际亏损4498万元,主营业务尚未真正盈利。 相比之下,康泰、康华、百克的盈利增长更多是来自产品销售。 康泰生物的利润修复,建立在去年的低基数之上;此外,研发费用同比降近四成,叠加2.49亿元理财相关收益,部分抵消了国内营收下滑的影响。 海外业务是增长的核心驱动力。前三季度收入1.02亿元,同比大增144%,已超过去年全年规模。 实现了产品出口、技术转移和产能共建。从市场来看,深耕东南亚、非洲、中东等新兴市场;印尼PCV13项目已实现本地化生产上市,7月水痘疫苗完成巴基斯坦首次供货,9月又签下埃及PCV20合作协议,产品梯队向高价次延伸,目前已覆盖20余个国家。 康华生物是唯一实现营收、利润、现金流同步正向增长的企业。 其核心大单品人二倍体细胞狂犬疫苗是主要驱动力,2026年截至10月签发了29批。前三季度销带动营收增5.31%。此外,销售、研发费用均同比收缩,财务费用延续利息净收入状态,整体期间费用率同比降4.59个百分点。 长远来看,将切入冻干mRNA技术平台,管线覆盖RSV、治疗性HPV等疫苗,为其第二增长曲线储备动力。 百克生物前三季度营收同比增18.84%,尚未实现正向盈利,但亏损幅度同比收窄。 其两大核心品种流感、带状疱疹疫苗下半年进入传统旺季。 2026年截至10月,签发的带状疱疹减毒活疫苗全部来自长春百克独家,合计12批。鼻喷流感减毒活疫苗,长春百克独家供应,合计12批。 同时水痘疫苗出口持续放量,销往印度、印尼等多国,贡献额外增量。 此外,存货、应收相关减值计提边际收窄,也减轻了利润拖累。当期唯一的拖累项是联营企业投资亏损同比扩大,前三季度多亏约709万元。 而欧林生物虽然由盈转亏,但主因是“补税”而非经营。其营收5.99亿元(+18.15%);归母净利润为-680.16万元,同比转亏(-114.33%);但是扣非净利润仍为正数。 公司收到税务部门《税务处理决定书》,需补缴税款及滞纳金共8740.80万元,其中本次补缴8320.79万元全部计入2026年当期损益。包括以前年度所得税调整约5226万元、滞纳金约3094万元。 records.content: Health Canada approves Moderna’s combined COVID, flu shot for some Both of the vaccines are only approved for Canadians aged 50 and older, and it's not clear yet when they might be available to get at your pharmacy. Health Canada has approved Moderna's combined influenza and COVID-19 vaccine as well its mRNA shot for seasonal influenza. Canada's top health agency says mFLUSIVA, an mRNA flu vaccine, as well as mCOFLU, a combination influenza and COVID-19 shot, can both now be used for adults 50 years of age and older. In August, the mRNA flu shot was approved for use in the United States and in April, the combination jab was approved for use in Europe, but Canada is the first country to approve both, Moderna said in a statement. "Health Canada's authorizations of mFLUSIVA and mCOFLU today mark another important step in bringing the benefits of mRNA technology to seasonal respiratory vaccination. It's not every day that a company gets two product approvals on the same day," Moderna CEO Stéphane Bancel said in a statement. It is unclear when the shots will be available for Canadians over 50 to get, but Moderna said it "will engage with Canadian health authorities and immunization partners as it advances plans for the future availability of mFLUSIVA and mCOFLU in Canada." The new flu shot and combination vaccine will not be part of the 2026-2027 immunization season, a spokesperson for Moderna told Global News. According to experts, mRNA-based vaccines have the potential to be more effective than traditional vaccines. Traditional flu vaccines use microbial protein or dead microbes to build protection against a disease. In contrast, mRNA vaccines give your cells a recipe they can use to produce proteins needed to fight the disease. They are typically considered fast-acting. "After injection, the cells in your arm muscles pick up the mRNA, make the protein, and display it on the cell's surface," the Vanderbilt University Medical Center website says. The National Advisory Committee on Immunization recommends that everyone six months of age and older get the non-mRNA flu shot that is available this year. A higher-dose version of the flu vaccine is recommended for adults aged 65 and older because aging immune systems often need a bigger boost. The committee also strongly advises COVID-19 vaccination for anyone 65 years of age and older and residents of long-term care, retirement homes or assisted living. –with files from The Canadian Press

records.content: 站内 得了甲流还会得乙流?中疾控最新研判:三毒株同时流行,没有交叉保护力 城市速递 2026年11月09日 07:22:22 来自北京市 今年的流感季确实有些不一样:H3N2、H1N1、乙流Victoria系三个毒株同时活跃。更值得警惕的是,不同流感毒株之间没有交叉保护力。感染过一次,换一种毒株可能还会再中招。 首都医科大学附属北京佑安医院感染综合科主任医师李侗曾在接受媒体采访时介绍,不同流感毒株之间无交叉保护力,三毒株共流行一方面可能增加短时间内先后感染不同毒株的风险,另一方面可能拉长流感季整体时长,推高总感染人数。 根据全国急性呼吸道传染病哨点监测情况,2026年10月26日—11月1日,全国哨点医院报告的流感样病例数占门急诊就诊总数的比例为4.1%,南方省份(4.8%)高于北方省份(3.3%)。 中国疾控中心分析,当前,全国大部分地区呼吸道传染病处于低水平,呈现小幅波动上升趋势。其中,流感活动呈波动上升趋势,A(H3N2)亚型、A(H1N1)亚型和B(Victoria)系流感病毒共同流行,A(H1N1)亚型占比上升;南北方省份流感活动水平差异显著,北方省份检测阳性率处于低流行水平,近期呈上升趋势,南方省份检测阳性率处于中流行水平;5~14岁病例组检测阳性率高于其他年龄组。 中国流感监测周报监测数据显示,10月26日—11月1日,全国检出流感阳性样本中甲型流感病毒占比65.4%、乙型流感病毒占比34.6%;甲型流感病毒中A(H1N1)pdm09占比51.2%、A(H3N2)占比48.8%,乙型流感病毒均为B(Victoria)系。 此外,10月26日—11月1日,全国共报告106起流感样病例暴发疫情。经检测,12起为A(H3N2),21起为A(H1N1)pdm09,7起为A型/甲型(亚型未显示),17起为B(Victoria),4起为B型/乙型(系未显示),23起为混合型,3起为流感阴性,19起暂未获得病原检测结果。 来源:光明日报全媒体记者王美莹,综合自中国疾病预防控制中心,封面图据图虫创意 本文来自大风号,仅代表大风号自媒体观点。 凤凰V现场 独家对话深蓝CEO姜海荣:大模型上车,车机正在告别“听指令” 德国IFA直击:中国企业如何用AI读懂一个家?2026中国联通合作伙伴大会在上海举行,九大成果看联通智能化布局华为Mate XT 2展翼三折叠深度体验:三折叠的新答案IFA 2026 ,安克硬控全场查看更多

新京报讯(记者戴轩)据我国最新一期流感监测周报,今年第44周,全国共报告106起流感样病例暴发疫情,其中23起为混合型。中疾控公布的监测数据显示,流感活动呈现波动上升,2种甲流、1种乙流亚型共同流行。 据中疾控公布的全国急性呼吸道传染病哨点监测情况,2026年第44周(10月26日-11月1日),对全国哨点医院(不含港澳台)采集的门急诊流感样病例和住院严重急性呼吸道感染病例的呼吸道样本,开展新型冠状病毒、流感病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒、腺病毒、人偏肺病毒、副流感病毒、普通冠状病毒、博卡病毒、鼻病毒和肠道病毒等10种病毒以及肺炎支原体在内的多种呼吸道病原体检测。 全国哨点医院报告的流感样病例数占门急诊就诊总数的比例(流感样病例百分比)为4.1%,南方省份(4.8%)高于北方省份(3.3%)。其中,216家开展呼吸道多病原监测的哨点医院门急诊流感样病例呼吸道样本检测阳性率前三位病原体为流感病毒(15.6%)、鼻病毒(11.4%)、人偏肺病毒(4.3%);住院严重急性呼吸道感染病例呼吸道样本检测阳性率前三位病原体为鼻病毒(10.1%)、流感病毒(6.1%)、人偏肺病毒(4.4%)。监测结果存在南北方地域差异和不同年龄段人群差异。 结合全国门急诊发热病例监测情况、哨点医院门急诊流感样病例就诊情况、多病原检测等监测结果分析显示,检出均为已知常见病原体,没有发现未知病原体及其导致的新发传染病。 流感活动呈波动上升趋势,A(H3N2)亚型、A(H1N1)亚型和B(Victoria)系流感病毒共同流行,A(H1N1)亚型占比上升;南北方省份流感活动水平差异显著,北方省份检测阳性率处于低流行水平,近期呈上升趋势,南方省份检测阳性率处于中流行水平;5~14岁病例组检测阳性率高于其他年龄组。鼻病毒检测阳性率在高位平台波动,14岁以下病例组检测阳性率较高。人偏肺病毒、副流感病毒和博卡病毒在0~4岁病例组检测阳性率较高。其他监测的呼吸道病原体阳性率处于低水平。 中国流感流行情况概要(截至2026年11月1日)显示,全国检出流感阳性样本中甲型流感病毒占比65.4%、乙型流感病毒占比34.6%;甲型流感病毒中A(H1N1)pdm09占比51.2%、A(H3N2)占比48.8%,乙型流感病毒均为B(Victoria)系。全国共报告106起流感样病例暴发疫情,经检测,12起为A(H3N2),21起为A(H1N1)pdm09,7起为A型(亚型未显示),17起为B(Victoria),4起为B型(系未显示),23起为混合型,3起为流感阴性,19起暂未获得病原检测结果。 当前,全国大部分地区呼吸道传染病处于低水平,呈现小幅波动上升趋势。为防范呼吸道传染病疫情,建议重点机构和场所做好健康监测,及时发现和处置聚集性疫情,公众采取以下个人防护措施: (1)积极主动接种疫苗:免疫力较弱人群(如孕妇、低龄儿童、老人及慢性病患者等)应根据疫苗接种指引接种预防呼吸道传染病的相关疫苗。 (2)科学佩戴口罩:在就医过程中需全程佩戴口罩;在人群密集场所或乘坐公共交通工具(如飞机、火车、地铁等)时建议佩戴口罩,尤其是老年人和一些有慢性基础性疾病的患者,以减少感染风险。 (3)保持良好卫生习惯:咳嗽或打喷嚏时,用纸巾、毛巾或手肘遮住口鼻;注意手卫生,避免用不洁净的手触摸眼、鼻、口,以减少病原体传播风险。 (4)倡导健康生活方式:要均衡饮食、适量运动和充足休息,增强身体免疫力。出现发热、咳嗽或其他呼吸道感染症状时,与人接触要佩戴口罩,保持室内良好通风;根据需要及时就医。 编辑 刘梦婕 校对 陈荻雁 10 +1 微博 微信 我要评论 登录 直播 直播中 直播|“首都开局起步‘十五五’”系列主题新闻发布会 760人参与 热点 1 宝洁携近百款新品亮相进博会:以数智赋能构建“未来消费品公司” 18.2万 records.content: 秋风渐凉 流感季 悄然而至 各地流感疫苗接种工作 也陆续展开 今年接种流感疫苗时 不少人发现 去年还是“四价”的流感疫苗 怎么变成“三价”了? 少了“一价” 效果会不会变差呢? 今年流行什么毒株? 据中国疾控中心监测,今年7月以来, 我国流感疫情呈现甲型H3N2亚型与乙型Victoria系共同流行的特征 ,其中甲型H3N2占比已超过乙型Victoria系。 中国疾控中心10月28日发布的流感监测周报(10月19日—25日)进一步显示: 👉全国检出流感阳性样本中甲型流感病毒占比67.6%、乙型流感病毒占比32.4%; 👉甲型中 A (H3N2) 占 67.2%、A (H1N1) pdm09 占 32.8%,乙型全部为 B (Victoria) 系,即 H3N2、H1N1、乙型 Victoria 三种毒株共同活跃 。 来源:中国疾控中心 专家提示, 我国流感高发时段多集中在11月~次年3月。 流感疫苗接种后,人体要经过2~4周才能生成足够的保护性抗体,现在正是接种流感疫苗的最佳时机。 三价流感疫苗 “够用”吗? 今年流感疫苗最大的变化是 “四价转三价”。 三价疫苗能否应对今年的毒株呢?专家介绍: 👉 三价流感疫苗: 覆盖两种甲型流感病毒H1N1和H3N2及乙型流感病毒Victoria系; 👉 四价流感疫苗: 在此基础上多覆盖一种乙型流感病毒Yamagata系。 由于乙型Yamagata系自2020年3月以来在全球再未被监测到,世界卫生组织建议将其从疫苗组分中移除。 2026至2027年度,世卫组织不再提供乙型Yamagata系的推荐毒株,全球流感疫苗全面调整为三价疫苗。 四价疫苗较三价疫苗在当前流行形势下,不具备更多优势,两种疫苗保护效果基本一致。 2026—2027年度,我国上市的三价流感疫苗包括 三价裂解疫苗、三价亚单位疫苗和三价减毒活疫苗。 ✅三价裂解疫苗和亚单位疫苗: 可以用于6月龄及以上的人群,包括0.25毫升和0.5毫升两种规格。 ✅三价减毒活疫苗: 适用于3~17岁的人群,每剂次0.2毫升。 专家提醒, 目前上市的流感疫苗均能有效预防流感 ,不用刻意追求价格、品牌、剂型,尽早完成接种最重要。 哪些人需要 接种流感疫苗? 很多人以为打流感疫苗是为了不得流感,其实它最核心的作用是 预防重症。 专家介绍, 人群对流感病毒普遍易感。 流感病毒感染可引起T细胞损伤与淋巴细胞耗竭,造成机体免疫功能受损。流感高危人群在此基础上更易继发细菌感染、诱发基础疾病恶化,部分病例可进展为重症。 建议所有6月龄及以上且无接种禁忌的人接种流感疫苗。 结合流感疫情形势和多病共防的防控策略,尽可能降低流感的危害,优先推荐以下重点和高风险人群接种: 👉医务人员,包括临床救治人员、公共卫生人员、卫生检疫人员等; 👉60岁及以上的老年人; 👉患一种或多种慢性病者; 👉养老机构、长期护理机构、福利院等人群聚集场所脆弱人群及员工; 👉6月龄及以上至5岁以下的儿童; 👉6月龄以下婴儿的家庭成员和看护人员; 👉托幼机构、中小学校、监管场所等重点场所人群; 👉孕妇。 接种流感疫苗 是 预防流感最经济 最有效的措施 主动接种疫苗 保护自己,也保护家人 来 源:中国疾控中心 国家应急广播 央视财经 广西疾控 编 辑:刘墨研 审 校:陈 孺 监 制:陈碧莹

records.content: 最近 你是不是发现身边发烧感冒的人增多 全国最新监测数据显示 门急诊流感样病例中 流感病毒阳性率排名第一 已位居呼吸道病原首位 最新一期的全国数据显示,门急诊收到的流感样病例中, 流感病毒阳性率已经排名第一,居各种呼吸道病原首位。 不过,总体流感样病例只占门急诊的3.8%,还属于零星散发情况。 据中国疾控中心最新流感监测周报(第43周,截至10月25日)显示, 全国检出流感阳性样本中甲型流感病毒占比67.6%、乙型流感病毒占比32.4%;甲型流感病毒中A(H1N1)pdm09 占比 32.8%、A(H3N2)占比67.2%,乙型流感病毒均为B(Victoria)系。全国共报告145起流感样病例暴发疫情, 而前一周报告仅为28起。目前, 秋冬流感流行季已逐渐开启 。从流行毒株看, 甲流为主、乙流为辅 。 (点击图片查看数据原文) 专家介绍,今年流感流行季的特点是: 多毒株共同活跃,流行节奏前移 。 上海交通大学医学院附属瑞金医院临床病毒研究室主任张欣欣介绍,当前流感处在低水平流行, 预计11月底至12月起进入上升通道。本轮主流毒株H3N2,感染者体感会更重。 张欣欣介绍,今年流感还有个特点,八九月就提前出现一波小高峰,病毒位点变异, 高龄老人、基础病患者感染后症状可能更重。 图片来源:AI生成 年轻人也扛不住! 本轮主打H3N2,症状偏重 26岁的张先生前段时间突然发烧、头痛、浑身难受,去上海瑞金医院检查,确诊感染H3N2亚型甲流。 他回想,一个月前得过一次小感冒没当回事,身体偏弱时病毒趁虚而入。 医生介绍,张先生是这阵收治到的流感患者中最年轻的。 流感不挑年纪,但会挑免疫力弱的人群。 即便是像张先生这样的年轻人,及时就医吃了特效药后, 完全康复依旧需要约两周时间, 更别提老人、儿童、孕产妇和有基础疾病的人群,万一引发肺炎、心肌炎等并发症,就更加棘手。对此,医生建议,流感还是要注重预防,提前接种流感疫苗是最简单有效的方式之一。 四川流感气象风险地图出炉 11月3日,四川省气象局、四川省疾控中心联合推出四川省流感气象风险预报产品,面向公众发布。采用气象指标和疾病指标构建精细化流感气象风险预测模型,将流感气象风险预报划分为低、较低、中等、较高、高5个等级,针对不同风险等级会提示相应的防范措施和建议,以降低流感发生风险。 10月四川省流感已达到中流行水平, 近期四川流感气象风险总体呈上升趋势 。 预计11月全省平均气温为11.4~11.9°C,较常年同期(10.9°C)偏高;平均降水量为20~25毫米,接近常年同期(22.8毫米),本月共有4次降温降水过程,需重点防范降温前后1至3天的传播高峰。 近期,根据四川省气象台最新预报,11月6日至8日有一次降温降水天气过程,盆地大部有小雨,西南部和南部局地有中雨,日平均气温将累计下降2~4°C。 健康风险提示 双毒株叠加感染会加重病情吗? 面对双毒株叠加感染会加重病情,首都医科大学附属北京佑安医院感染综合科主任医师李侗曾表示,双毒株同时感染后的症状确实 会比单一毒株感染更重,但同时感染的概率低 。 相比之下, 短时间内两次感染的情况更可能出现 , 即先感染一种毒株,康复后又感染另一种毒株, “反复感染会造成明显身体损伤,需重点防范。” 现在打流感疫苗晚不晚? 我国流感高发期一般是11月到次年3月, 整个流感季都可以接种疫苗 ,最佳接种时机是9、10月份。早打比晚打好,晚打比不打好。 建议6月龄及以上人群 , 尤其是老人、儿童、慢性病患者等重点人群,以及学校、养老机构、福利院等重点场所人员, 在当地流感流行季来临前尽早接种流感疫苗 。 流感疫苗怎么选? 根据中国疾控中心发布的《中国流感疫苗预防接种技术指南(2026—2027)》,本年度推荐的三种疫苗组分均进行了更新,包括三价裂解疫苗、三价亚单位疫苗和三价减毒活疫苗。 三价裂解疫苗和亚单位疫苗 可以用于6月龄及以上的人群,包括0.25毫升和0.5毫升两种规格。 三价减毒活疫苗 适用于3到17岁的人群,每剂次0.2毫升。 值得关注的是,2026—2027流感流行季, 四川省针对农村地区65周岁及以上老年人和义务教育阶段在校中小学生,免费提供1剂次三价流感病毒裂解疫苗接种服务。 详情点击查看👉免费福利!事关乐山农村地区“一老一小” 服用抗流感病毒药 能代替接种流感疫苗吗? 两者属于不同的保护途径: 1.接种流感疫苗 可以刺激机体产出针对流感病毒的特异性抗体, 提供长达数月的持续保护 , 属于主动免疫。 2.服用抗病毒药物 一般不用于常规预防,仅在重症高危人群作为流感患者密切接触者,且未接种疫苗或接种后尚未获得免疫力时,可在暴露后48小时内遵医嘱进行 短期的暴露后预防 , 该措施属于应急性的临时手段。 因此, 接种流感疫苗是预防流感的第一道防线,抗流感病毒药不能代替疫苗接种。 这两种情况 不要在家硬扛 1. 怀疑对乙酰氨基酚 服用过量。 哪怕暂时没有不适,也应立即就医。不要等到皮肤、眼白发黄再处理。 2. 流感患者如果出现 呼吸困难、持续胸痛胸闷、意识异常、尿量明显减少 ,或 症状好转后又加重 , 应及时就医。 流感季已至 早接种、早防护 别等“中招”才后悔 转发提醒更多人! 消息综合: 中国疾控中心、新闻坊、 央视新闻、 人民日报健康客户端等
